Computing & programming

delete verb

also erase, remove (a file), rub out, erasure, crossing-out

classical

Mart. 14.7.2
Traupman 260, 302

dēleō, dēlēre, dēlēvī, dēlētum

verb, second conjugation

wipe out, erase

The classical verb for rubbing writing off a wax tablet, and Traupman’s for deleting on a computer: the sense has not moved.

Other words

  • expungō, expungere, expūnxī, expūnctum — strike out (from a list)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · M-O s.v. delete

    Classically to strike a name off a list by pricking dots against it (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens cites a scholar of 1698 who struck out false entries from a dictionary.

  • ērādō, ērādere, ērāsī, ērāsum — scratch out, erase

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Tac. A. 4.42 (Lewis & Short): aliquem albō ērādere; Traupman 29; Traupman 310

    Scraping writing off a tablet or a list; Lewis & Short: ante-classical and from Augustus on.

  • litūra, litūrae f. — an erasure, a crossing-out

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Arch. 9: ūnīus nōminis litūra (Lewis & Short); Traupman 29; Traupman 310

    The smoothed wax where something written has been rubbed out.

Examples

  • esse putā cērās, licet haec membrāna vocētur: dēlēbis, quotiēns scrīpta novāre volēs

    think of it as wax, though it is called parchment: you will rub it out whenever you want to write afreshMart. 14.7.1–2

See also document, backup.
